title: Decide what tk upgrade's factory staleness warning becomes
description:
SMALL AND INDEPENDENT — it does not depend on the split's shape, so it can run alongside the design tick.

cmd/tk/cmd/upgrade.go:65-80 loads ~/.ticksrc, and if KeyFactoryURL is set, compares KeyFactoryVersion against the release being installed to warn that the user's deployed factory is behind. It is the clearest surviving ticks->factory coupling in a core command: tk upgrade knows what a factory is, what version it runs, and that it can be stale.

DECIDE, and any of these can be right:
- It moves to ticfac. 'ticfac upgrade' or a staleness check the factory does itself is the natural home once ticfac owns its own deployment.
- It disappears. Nobody has ever deployed a factory from a release — tk factory has never shipped in any tag — so this warning has fired for exactly one person, on dev builds.
- It survives generically. tk upgrade warns about ANY registered companion tool that declares a deployed version, knowing nothing about factories. More machinery than the problem probably deserves; include it only if you think it earns its place.

The bar is the project's rule: ticks ends with zero factory couplings. A warning that names a factory is a coupling however small, so 'keep it as is' is not on the list.

Implement the decision, do not just record it. If it moves to ticfac, the destination is cloud/factory or internal/factory — both leave in Phase 5, so putting it there is putting it in the right repo already.
acceptance_criteria: cmd/tk/cmd/upgrade.go contains no reference to a factory, and does not read KeyFactory* anything. The chosen disposition is implemented and its reasoning recorded at the site or in the extraction spec. If the warning survives anywhere, it works. go test ./cmd/... green.
